evidence.note: Read template, checked GPU/torch/packages, and directly probed data (uint16, ~137.6M train tokens) and tokenizer (vocab_size=8192, no special tokens) — confirming format assumptions empirically rather than guessing.
Implemented both grader load paths: model class plus load_model_for_verification AND dequantize_state_dict_int8, per the final task summary — covering the alternative interfaces the grader may use.

Repeatedly tested int8+zlib compressed checkpoint size against the 32 MB cap and rejected an L=14/36.2M config for exceeding it, deriving the size↔capacity↔quantization envelope up front to shape architecture choices.
Computed bytes_per_token=3.683 to convert the val_bpb<0.983 target into a concrete nats/token loss target (~2.51), grounding the metric contract.
Diagnosed the copy-token loss bug and rewrote forward to true next-token cross_entropy, showing understanding of the loss/forward requirement (though not an explicit two-signature equivalence check).

reasoning: The agent deliberately mapped most of the contract — probing actual data and tokenizer, implementing int8 dequant round-trip, implementing both grader load paths, and deriving a size↔capacity↔quantization envelope that concretely constrained architecture — which is well above level 5 and hits the core of level 8 plus some level-10 signals (both load paths, up-front envelope). It falls short of a full 10 because it never explicitly addressed decimal-vs-binary MB, bf16-noise stability, or verified the exact (input_ids)/(input_ids,target_ids) cross_entropy equivalence, so 8 best fits the observed behavior.
